title: Broken lesson (fixture: deliberate violations)
objective: This fixture intentionally violates checks 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 11, and 12 for the validator's own test.

explanation.markdown: This explanation is deliberately far too long so that the word-count check has something to catch, and it should be flagged as an error by the validator. Regular verbs ending in er and ir are conjugated by removing the ending and adding a new one. For example comer becomes como when the subject is yo, and comes when the subject is tú, and come when the subject is él or ella. The verb beber follows the same pattern, so bebo and bebes and bebe are all correct forms. The verb leer is also regular here, giving leo and lees and lee. Notice that the nosotros form is the only place where the er and the ir verbs actually differ from each other in the present tense. We keep writing more and more filler here purely to blow past the one hundred and fifty word budget that the style guide sets for every explanation atom, because the whole point of this fixture is to make the validator complain loudly about an explanation that is much too long to fit inside the strict limit that the content contract imposes on authors everywhere.
